definitions.explanation: A train heading away from Tokyo or a major city.
A particular part or passage in a text.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}の{下|くだ}りは{足|あし}が{痛|いた}くなる。
examples.english: My legs hurt on the way down the mountain.

examples.japanese: {上|のぼ}りより{下|くだ}りのほうが{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: The descent took longer than the climb.

examples.japanese: この{道|みち}は{下|くだ}りがきついから、{気|き}をつけて{歩|ある}いたほうがいい。
examples.english: The descent on this road is steep, so you should walk carefully.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{下|くだ}りは{人|ひと}が{少|すく}ない。
examples.english: There are few people on the morning down-train.

examples.japanese: {東京|とうきょう}から{大阪|おおさか}に{向|む}かう{新幹線|しんかんせん}は{下|くだ}りで、その{逆|ぎゃく}は{上|のぼ}りだ。
examples.english: A bullet train heading from Tokyo to Osaka is a down-train, and the reverse is an up-train.

examples.japanese: この{下|くだ}りが{好|す}きだ。
{面白|おもしろ}い{下|くだ}りがある。
この{小説|しょうせつ}のこの{下|くだ}りが{一番|いちばん}{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: This passage of this novel is my favorite.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{手紙|てがみ}のあの{下|くだ}りを{読|よ}んで{泣|な}いた。
examples.english: I cried reading that passage of his letter.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}は{本|ほん}のある{下|くだ}りを{読|よ}み{上|あ}げて、それについて{説明|せつめい}してくれた。
examples.english: The teacher read aloud a passage from the book and explained it to us.

notes:
{下|くだ}り is the noun form of {下|くだ}る (to go down).

TRAIN TERMINOLOGY:
- {下|くだ}り: down-train (away from Tokyo/major city)
- {上|のぼ}り: up-train (toward Tokyo/major city)
- {下|くだ}り{線|せん}: down-line (track)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {下|くだ}りの{電車|でんしゃ} (down-train)
- {坂|さか}の{下|くだ}り (going downhill)

ANTONYM:
- {上|のぼ}り (going up, up-train)
